verdict.rationale: Ardent's API authentication docs show role-scoped tokens, such as a read-only role_org_viewer for automation. The agent workflow docs describe giving an agent only a branch URL that needs no Ardent token, can't touch anything but its branch and has zero access to the source database. That is real least-privilege scoping, but token scoping is only evidenced at the org-role level, with one role shown. missing for 10: documentation of the full role set and of issuing tokens scoped to a project, connector or branch; token expiry and revocation controls; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: The agent needs no Ardent token and can't touch anything but its branch.
If a branch URL is ever compromised, it has zero access to your original database. This makes it safe to hand branch URLs to AI agents
Set ARDENT_TOKEN and run commands normally — no login step
